title: Day-zero activation credit architectures
content:
Purpose
Quick, rough thinking about Day-0 / Day-1 credit architectures we can seed to new users to drive meaningful product usage while protecting unit economics. Trying to balance: low friction -> good retention signal vs cost blowouts from imaginative early usage.

Goals / constraints
- Incentivize the first 3–7 high-quality sessions (conversations or key API calls) so user sees value.
- Avoid huge one-off consumption (eg. long-generation abuse) while still letting devs prototype.
- Make the redemption rules easy to understand and instrumentable.
- Keep expected cost per converted paying customer under target (back-of-envelope target: $25 CAC credit spend).

Assumptions (ballpark numbers to do math)
- Baseline infra cost per 1M tokens served (amortized full-stack) ~ $12 (includes GPU time, network, infra ops). This implies ~ $0.000012 per token.
- Typical interactive session = 2k tokens roundtrip (prompt + responses combined). Session cost ~ $0.024.
- Average new user uses 6 sessions in first week if engaged. Total tokens ~ 12k -> $0.144 cost.
- Conversion rate from free-trial engaged cohort -> paid: 3.5% (target cohort after onboarding).
- Allowable credit spend per new user (to stay under credit-acquisition CAC target) ~ $0.75/user seeded, if we assume 70% organic and 30% paid acquisition mix. These are knobs.

Credit architecture ideas (sketches)
1) Session-bucket credits (deterministic)
   - Seed 5 "session credits". Each session credit = 2k tokens (or capped at 2k).
   - Pros: predictable spend (~5 * $0.024 = $0.12/user), easy to explain, encourages trying multiple integrations.
   - Cons: users with many short sessions get more than useful; users doing single long session limited.

2) Token-chunk credits with per-call cap (hybrid)
   - Seed 10 chunks of 1k tokens. Per-call cap of 3 chunks (3k tokens). Expiry 30d.
   - Predicted cost: 10 * $0.012 = $0.12/user. Allows a couple of longer tests but caps single-call abuse.
   - Notes: simplest to map to cost model if our billing is token-based.

3) Use-case driven envelopes (guided onboarding)
   - Offer 3 envelopes: "chat prototype" (10k tokens), "ingest + search" (5k embedding units + 2k tokens), "rerank test" (3k tokens). User selects one path on signup.
   - Expected deployment cost differs by path; surface expected remaining credit per path. Keeps user focused and gives better signal about product fit.

4) Half-life decay credits (behavioral anchoring)
   - Seed large initial pool (e.g., 20k tokens), but credit value decays: each week unused credit loses 50% of face value. Forces early exploration.
   - Example: user sees 20k token credit day0, but if they do nothing in week1 it becomes 10k then 5k, etc.
   - Upside: encourages early activation. Downside: harder to explain; perceived as punitive.

5) Milestone-based top-ups (event signaling)
   - Give small base credit (5k tokens). Offer additional one-off top-ups for completing key onboarding milestones (connect Slack, call API once with real key, run eval test).
   - Each milestone top-up = 3k tokens. This ties credits to meaningful signals and limits wasting credits on random experiments.

Quick unit-econ sketches (scenarios)
Scenario A: Session-bucket default
- Seed 5 session credits (2k/session) -> $0.12/user
- Activation funnel: 40% try at least 1 session, 18% do 3+, 3.5% convert -> effective credit spend per converted user = $0.12 / 0.035 = $3.43. (far below $25 target, safe)
- If marketing pushes a lot of non-target users, realized spend could go up; cap via per-account throttle.

Scenario B: Token-chunk generous
- Seed 20k tokens flat -> $0.24/user
- Same conversion funnel -> $6.86 per converted user. Still okay but risk of single-user heavy use increases tail costs.

Scenario C: Milestone-driven (higher intent)
- Seed 5k base + 2 milestone top-ups expected (not all users trigger them) -> avg spend ~$0.18/user
- If milestones successfully correlate to conversion (eg users who earn both top-ups convert at 12%), CAC credit per converted = $0.18 / 0.12 = $1.50. Much better.

Abuse controls and guardrails
- Per-call token cap (e.g., 4k tokens) while on credit to prevent single long-run blast.
- Rate limits (tokens/sec per key) and aggregate daily caps on credit consumption (e.g., 30k tokens/day).
- Heuristics to flag suspicious accounts (same IP, high entropy queries) and quarantine credit redemption.
- Require billing card on file after X days or after N tokens consumed to reduce freebie churn and enable throttled upgrades.

Signals to measure (minimal instrumentation list)
- Day-0 -> Day-7 sessions per user, tokens consumed per session distribution.
- Fraction of users hitting milestone gates (if using milestone flow).
- Conversion rate by entry path (which envelope selected, or whether milestone triggered).
- Cost per converted user attributable to credits (sum credits used / # conversions).
- Tail risk: top 1% of free accounts account for what % of credit spend? Aim < 30%.

Operational notes / rollout plan (MVP)
1) Start with Session-bucket credits (5 sessions @ 2k) + per-call cap 4k + 30k/day aggregate limit. Low implementation complexity.
2) Instrument conversion metrics and tail usage for 30 days.
3) If tail pronounced, shift to milestone top-ups: replace static seeds with guided onboarding flows that require an API call or integration.
4) Experiment: variant test of token-chunks vs session-buckets (A/B) with 10k cohort each to measure activation lift and CAC-credit spend.

Open questions / design tradeoffs
- Do we require billing card on sign-up or only after credit exhaustion? (Card on file reduces abuse but is a funnel drop.)
- Are we comfortable with per-user seeded cost up to $1 in organic channels if conversion lifts by X%? Need clear ROI threshold.
- UX clarity: "You have X tokens" vs "You have Y sessions" — which drives behavior better for developers?
- Multi-product bundles: if a new user tries embeddings + chat, how to apportion credits? Simple approach: separate envelopes or tag usage to envelope selected.

Immediate to-dos
- Prod: instrument token-by-path metrics and per-account credit spend histogram. (Eng ticket)
- Growth: draft two onboarding flows copy for session-bucket vs milestone top-ups. (Draft UX copy)
- Finance: sanity check assumed infra $/M-token figure vs current amortized dashboard.

Raw calcs scratch (easy to copy/paste)
- cost_per_token = 12 / 1_000_000 = 0.000012
- session_tokens = 2000 -> session_cost = 2000 * cost_per_token = 0.024
- session_bucket_5_cost = 5 * session_cost = 0.12
- credit_cac = session_bucket_5_cost / conversion_rate -> 0.12 / 0.035 = 3.43

Notes to self: keep the first experiment simple, measure fast. The milestone/top-up approach looks promising because it ties spend to signals we actually care about (real integration/use). But UX needs to be simple and explicit so users understand why they get incrementally more credit.

End.
